Music Synthesizer for Android (MSFA): a six-operator FM synthesis engine.

Source: https://github.com/google/music-synthesizer-for-android
        (app/src/main/jni)
Commit: f67d41d313b7dc85f6fb99e79e515cc9d208cfff (2017-09-12)
License: Apache-2.0, see LICENSE (Copyright 2012 Google Inc.)

No MSFA file is kept here. audiofm's kernel is adapted from these files and
lives in src/shared, where each adapted file keeps the Apache-2.0 notice and
says what changed:

  src/shared/audiodsp_fm.c, audiodsp_fm.h
      from dx7note.cc/.h, env.cc/.h, lfo.cc/.h, pitchenv.cc/.h,
      fm_core.cc/.h, fm_op_kernel.cc/.h, exp2.h, sin.h, freqlut.cc,
      patch.cc and synth_unit.cc
  src/shared/audiodsp_fm_tables.h, written by tools/fm_tables.py
      from the table set-up in sin.cc and exp2.cc

The changes, in short: C instead of C++; per-synth rather than global
sample-rate tables; constant sine and exp2 tables; feedback loops that span
two or three operators; transpose, oscillator key sync, operator on/off,
amplitude modulation, the mod wheel, a pitch-bend range, voice stealing and
an end-of-note test; parameters clamped before any table lookup; and the
voice packing written in both directions. The NEON kernels, the resonant
filter and the MIDI and ring-buffer plumbing are not used.

tools/fm_tables.py --check confirms the generated header is current;
its sine and exp2 tables equal MSFA's runtime tables value for value.
